# Disagreement Log — Apocalypse of Peter, Chapter 11
**Agents:** EMET | LOGOS | PNEUMA
**Total Disagreements:** 12

---

## Verse-by-Verse Disagreements

### v.1 — "dark and gloomy one" vs. "darker, more oppressive, heavier with gloom" (PNEUMA)
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "dark and gloomy"
- **PNEUMA:** "darker, more oppressive, heavier with gloom"
- **Note:** PNEUMA expands a two-word description into a three-phrase elaboration. Not in source.

### v.4 — "ate and drank with the body of Christ" vs. "ate and drank the body of Christ"
- **EMET:** "ate and drank with the body of Christ" (instrumental)
- **LOGOS/PNEUMA:** "ate and drank the body of Christ" (direct object)
- **Note:** The preposition "with" (EMET) may reflect the Ethiopic more literally; the direct object form (LOGOS) reflects the Eucharistic theology more clearly. Theologically significant.

### v.4 — "in a hypocritical manner" vs. "in pretense and hypocrisy" (PNEUMA)
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "in a hypocritical manner"
- **PNEUMA:** "in pretense and hypocrisy"
- **Note:** PNEUMA doubles the concept. Source has one term.

### v.5 — "crowns of flame" vs. "crowns of fire"
- **EMET:** "crowns of flame"
- **LOGOS/PNEUMA:** "crowns of fire"
- **Note:** "Flame" vs. "fire" — minor. "Fire" (LOGOS) is preferred as it matches the repeated *pur* throughout.

### v.7 — "had the priestly office" vs. "held the priestly office" vs. "received the office"
- **EMET:** "had the priestly office"
- **LOGOS:** "held the priestly office"
- **PNEUMA:** "received the office"
- **Note:** "Held" (LOGOS) implies proper possession with responsibility attached. Minor.

### v.7 — "not served aright" vs. "not served faithfully" vs. "corrupted what was given to them" (PNEUMA)
- **EMET:** "not served aright"
- **LOGOS:** "not served faithfully"
- **PNEUMA:** "they never served as they should have. They corrupted what was given to them."
- **Note:** PNEUMA's "corrupted" is an addition beyond the source's simple "did not serve aright."

### v.8 — "consuming fire" vs. "fire eating out of their mouths" (PNEUMA)
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "fire consuming their mouths" / "mouths consuming fire"
- **PNEUMA:** "flames eating out of their mouths"
- **Note:** "Eating out of their mouths" reverses the direction — fire eating out rather than fire consuming the mouth inward. Minor but real directional difference.

### v.10 — "perverted justice and who had judged unjustly"
- **EMET:** "had perverted justice and who had judged unjustly"
- **LOGOS:** "perverted justice and judged unjustly"
- **PNEUMA:** "had the law in their hands and twisted it. Unjust judges — every verdict they delivered was a perversion."
- **Note:** PNEUMA's elaboration ("every verdict... a perversion") is not in source.

### v.11 — "set snares against the righteous" vs. "set traps for the righteous"
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "set snares against the righteous"
- **PNEUMA:** "set traps for the righteous"
- **Note:** "Snares" (EMET/LOGOS) is the biblical term (*pagida*); "traps" is equivalent but loses the scriptural resonance.

### v.14 — "did not remember God" vs. "never once kept God in mind" (PNEUMA)
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "did not remember God"
- **PNEUMA:** "who never once kept God in mind"
- **Note:** "Never once" is PNEUMA's intensifier. "Did not remember God" is a formal Hebrew/Ethiopic phrase (*lo' zakar*-equivalent).

### v.15 — "great mill" vs. "great millstone"
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "great mill"
- **PNEUMA:** "great millstone"
- **Note:** The source specifies a mill (*tahana*) not just a millstone. "Mill" (EMET/LOGOS) is more accurate.

### v.17 — "grinders of the poor" — all agents agree
- **PNEUMA** adds "And it was enough" as a literary comment — not a translation issue, but a narrative intrusion.
- **Note:** PNEUMA's "And it was enough" is a narrative interpretation appended to the angel's words. Not in source; removed by SOPHIA.

---
*12 disagreements. SOPHIA: "ate and drank the body of Christ" (v.4); "crowns of fire" (v.5); "set snares" (v.11); "great mill" (v.15); remove PNEUMA's "And it was enough" (v.17).*
